title: The truncation triangle tau_{<=q-1}K -> tau_{<=q}K -> H^q(K)[-q] is distinguished
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category with derived category $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], cohomology functors $H^n$ and shift $[1]$, $(M[1])^r=M^{r+1}$, $d_{M[1]}=-d_M$. For a complex $K$ of $\mathcal A$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$ let $\tau_{\leq q}K$ be the canonical truncation, the subcomplex $\cdots\to K^{q-2}\to K^{q-1}\to\Ker(d^q_K)\to0\to\cdots$ of $K$ (the truncation of the standard t-structure [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]), so that $\tau_{\leq q-1}K\subseteq\tau_{\leq q}K$, and let $H^q(K)[-q]$ be the complex with the single object $H^q(K)$ placed in degree $q$. Let $i_q:\tau_{\leq q-1}K\to\tau_{\leq q}K$ be the inclusion and $j_q:\tau_{\leq q}K\to H^q(K)[-q]$ the morphism of complexes which in degree $q$ is the projection $\Ker(d^q_K)\to H^q(K)$ and zero in the other degrees. Then there is a unique morphism $k_q:H^q(K)[-q]\to(\tau_{\leq q-1}K)[1]$ in $D(\mathcal A)$ such that
$$
 \tau_{\leq q-1}K\xrightarrow{\,i_q\,}\tau_{\leq q}K\xrightarrow{\,j_q\,}H^q(K)[-q]\xrightarrow{\,k_q\,}(\tau_{\leq q-1}K)[1]
$$
is a distinguished triangle of $D(\mathcal A)$ (namely $k_q=\delta\circ\bar j_q^{-1}$, where $\delta$ is the boundary morphism of the distinguished triangle of the short exact sequence of complexes $0\to\tau_{\leq q-1}K\to\tau_{\leq q}K\to\tau_{\leq q}K/\tau_{\leq q-1}K\to0$ and $\bar j_q:\tau_{\leq q}K/\tau_{\leq q-1}K\to H^q(K)[-q]$ is the quasi-isomorphism induced by $j_q$). The triangle is functorial in $K$: a morphism $K\to L$ of $D(\mathcal A)$ induces a morphism of triangles. If $K$ is bounded below, so are the three terms; in particular for $\mathcal A=\Ab(T_{\Et})$ the triangle lies in $\Dplus(T_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories].

source.place: Derived Categories, Remark 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle, line 4076): the canonical distinguished triangle tau_{<=a}K -> tau_{<=a+1}K -> H^{a+1}(K)[-a-1] -> (tau_{<=a}K)[1], from the short exact sequence of truncations and the quasi-isomorphism to H^{a+1}(K)[-a-1]; here a=q-1
